name: Fried Yuca With Spicy Mayo

ingredients.name: jalapeño pepper, stems and seeds removed, roughly chopped
grated cotija, romano, or feta cheese

instructions.primary_message: Peel yuca, split in half crosswise, and cut into 1.5 to 2-cm thick batons. Place in a pot and cover with cold water by 5 cm. Season well with salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, reduce to a simmer, and cook until tender and yuca is starting to fray, about 15 minutes. Drain.

While yuca is cooking, combine mayonnaise, aji amarillo, lime juice, jalapeño, cilantro, and cheese in the jar of a blender and blend on high speed until smooth. Alternatively, blend in a up with a hand blender. Season to taste with salt if necessary. Set aside.

When yuca is boiled, heat oil to 175°C (350°F) in a fryer, Dutch oven, or large wok over high heat. Adjust flame to maintain temperature. Add yuca and cook, agitating and flipping frequently, until golden brown and crisp, about 3 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel-lined tray and shake to drain. Season with salt. Serve immediately with sauce for dipping.

schema_metadata.keywords: colombian cuisine, fries, Latin American cuisine, latin cuisine, peruvian cuisine, yuca

description: Fried yuca is like the crispier, creamier version of french fries. Ours is served with a sweet, hot, and tangy mayo for dipping.
notes:
Optional substitutions: peanut oil → vegetable oil

Notes: Aji amarillo is a sweet yellow chile paste that can be found in most Latin markets with Peruvian ingredients. It can be omitted or replaced with a few dashes of your favorite hot sauce.
author: J. Kenji López-Alt
